deviations.affects: trajectory recompilation only. Outcomes, counts, corpus items, splits, observations and retrieval rankings all reproduce.
deviations.detail: compilation_id is derived from the task and its ordered source events, so the W3 rows cannot be recompiled to match after the W6-F1 fix: their created_at is the moment the operator ran the campaign. They are left as recorded history rather than deleted or rewritten, on the same reasoning as W3-D2. A campaign on a clean store reproduces exactly; recompilation of these sixty rows will keep refusing, and that refusal is correct behaviour reporting a real difference.
deviations.title: the sixty trajectory manifests compiled in W3 keep a wall-clock created_at and are not rewritten

findings.detail: scripts/reality_campaign.py passed created_at=utc_now() into reality_trajectories.build_request. ExperienceCompilerService verifies a persisted manifest by recompiling the request and comparing for exact equality, and created_at is the manifest's only field not derived from the task and its outcomes. A resume therefore failed all sixty compilations with 'persisted manifest differs from deterministic recompilation'. Fixed by passing the campaign epoch, the same fix W3-F2 applied to corpus requests.
findings.title: trajectory compilation read a wall clock, so no trajectory could be verified by recompilation

findings.detail: tests/integration/postgres/conftest.py TRUNCATEs the whole cognitive_os schema and guarded only on the database name ending in `_test`. The C3 evidence store is also named `..._test`, so putting the PostgreSQL integration suite into the release matrix under the C3 environment destroyed the campaign evidence. Several unit suites additionally write into whatever COGOS_DATABASE_URL and COGOS_ARTIFACT_ROOT name, so the contamination was wider than the truncation. Fixed in three places: the fixture now requires the database to be nominated by name in COGOS_TRUNCATABLE_DATABASE and skips with a reason when nothing is nominated; the matrix gives every test row a scratch database and a scratch artifact root and refuses when the scratch handle names the evidence store; CI nominates its own throwaway service database.
findings.impact: no data was lost: both wipes were recovered in full from the backup taken by S21C3-062 minutes earlier.
findings.recovery: pg_restore of 20260730T163758Z-event-store.dump plus the matching artifact tar; every count returned to its pre-incident value.
findings.regression_test: tests/cognitive_os/coding/test_reality_operations.py and the fixture's own refusal, exercised in three states (unnominated, mismatched, nominated).
findings.title: the release matrix erased the C3 evidence store, twice, and the guard that should have stopped it only checked a naming convention
